prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

TEXT_G:
Summary (≤500 words; policy-focused, non-ideological)

Core objective and process
- Withdraw from the European Union by repealing the European Communities Act, ending budget contributions, restoring UK legal primacy, and regaining an independent seat at bodies like the WTO.
- Two-year transition managed by a cabinet committee to review, repeal, or replace EU-derived laws and to create UK policies for agriculture, fisheries, trade, and other areas.

Economy and regulation
- Maintain tariff-free/bilateral trade with European neighbors, pursue broader global trade links (Commonwealth, North America, Asia), and cooperate on shared issues (environment, residence rights).
- Systematic deregulation with a presumption to scrap rules unless clearly necessary, prioritizing relief for small businesses; remove measures such as the Working Time Directive.
- Use the claimed c. £1bn/year saved from EU contributions to raise the state pension by £2/week; temporarily increase borrowing by £3bn/year for immediate tax cuts and targeted spending, notably on defense.
- Immediate tax changes: halve council tax for all households; abolish the 10% income tax band; reinstate dividend tax credits for pension funds; raise the inheritance tax threshold to £500,000.
- Longer term: simplify and lower taxes, replace VAT with a wholesale sales tax, merge National Insurance with income tax, and consider a flat tax.

Health, welfare, and pensions
- Decentralize NHS management; cap bureaucracy; restore a single accountable clinical manager (“matron”) model; scrap Strategic Health Authorities; reopen GP surgeries evenings/weekends; ease target-driven constraints on clinicians; consider complementary private insurance; remove EU limits on supplements/herbals and the Working Time Directive in health.
- Simplify and reduce means-testing in benefits; prioritize transparency and work incentives; avoid large-scale “active labour market” programs without proven outcomes.
- Pensions: raise state pensions by £2/week (via EU savings); reinstate pension fund tax credits (~£5bn/year); restore full uprating for expatriate pensioners; acknowledge need for higher saving/longer working over time.

Education
- Grant greater school autonomy; scrap SATs; empower heads to exclude; provide specialist provision for excluded pupils; allow limited selection and specialisms; emphasize sport, trips, and core standards; remove central interference in exam standards.
- Expand access to independent schooling via assisted places, vouchers, or tax reliefs.
- Universities: review and defund low-standard courses; fully fund high-standard courses; cancel top-up fees; provide maintenance grants; scrap student loans; charge EU students full overseas rates; expand technical colleges.

Law and order and immigration
- Increase local accountability of police; reduce paperwork; strengthen magistrates; review sentencing with clear minima and maxima; build prisons as needed; protect homeowners defending property.
- Target near zero net immigration: introduce a points-based system; equal treatment for EU and non-EU applicants; tighter family reunification; reinstate embarkation controls; language/civics tests; health checks; redefine and strictly apply refugee criteria (no claims via safe third countries); accelerate removals.

Agriculture and fisheries
- Replace CAP with guaranteed minimum prices/deficiency payments; reduce bureaucracy; improve biosecurity; reopen small abattoirs; support local food, green/hill farming, young farmers; consider restoring the Milk Marketing Board.
- Exit the CFP; reassert control over UK waters; strengthen enforcement; regulate gear/mesh; use fallow zones for stock recovery.

Defense and foreign affairs
- Maintain NATO alignment; disengage from EU defense structures; retain independent international representation; reverse force cuts; increase defense spending; prioritize domestic procurement; deploy only for clear national interest.

Energy, environment, and transport
- Halt wind turbine rollout; build new nuclear fission plants; invest in fusion R&D; develop clean-coal technologies.
- Set environmental policy domestically; prioritize recycling, habitat protection, green farming; restrict GM crop planting until long-term safety is proven.
- Continue rail upgrades; consider reintegrating track and train management; resist EU transport directives; increase road investment; localize traffic management; raise some speed limits where safe; limit speed cameras to proven danger sites.

Governance
- Preserve existing national institutions; oppose further dilution of the revising chamber’s independence.
- Citizen-initiated referendums: if 5% of the electorate signs within six months, a binding national referendum is held.
- Consider “English-only” legislative days at Westminster; abolish English regional assemblies and related quangos.
- Redirect business rates and some duties to local councils; increase local autonomy and transparency; reduce politically driven posts; promote recycling.
- Repeal the Human Rights Act; maintain ECHR principles; drop ID cards; repeal the Hunting Act.

TEXT_D:
Scope
- Applies mainly to England due to devolution. Scottish and Welsh proposals may differ.

Fiscal approach and tax
- Reprioritise about £5bn annually by abolishing certain subsidies and departments/functions, cancelling ID cards, and diverting Child Trust Fund money to education.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate only on earnings above £100,000 to fund: abolition of university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; and cutting local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay.
- Independent scrutiny of budgets by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Typical household local tax bill reduced by about £450 under Local Income Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via expanded access to scans/tests, weekend/evening operation, and staffing/training.
- Free eye and dental checks; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- More clinicians; scrap central targets; more local accountability.
- NHS dentistry contract reform and personal dental plans.
- Health MOTs, personal care plans for long‑term conditions, stronger mental health rights, end age discrimination.
- Public health: school nutrition standards, limit junk‑food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund budget to hire 21,000 teachers; infant classes average 20, junior 25; extended school hours; 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Subject-specialist teaching in core subjects; reduce high‑stakes testing at 7 and 11; stronger SEN support; behaviour plans and managed transfers.
- Unified academic/vocational diplomas from 14; fund parity for colleges; maintain statutory school transport distances.
- Green building standards for education estates; strengthen outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders and equality
- 10,000 more police (funded by scrapping ID cards) plus complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy, modernise tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences; anti‑social behaviour tools with underlying support.
- Prisons focused on work, literacy and skills; progress tied to effort.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; tighten judicial control of any control orders; allow intercept evidence; repeal flawed terror provisions.
- Overhaul asylum processing via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; pursue EU common standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units in every force.

Economy and business
- Stamp Duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simpler, lighter regulation with impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small‑business rate relief and site‑value rating; fair‑trading duty; English Tourism Board.
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for cleaner vehicles and energy‑efficient homes.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no replacement of aging nuclear plants.

Pensions, benefits and family support
- From 75: basic state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; residency‑based “citizen’s pension.”
- Replace Council Tax to benefit most pensioners; six months’ maternity pay at minimum‑wage rate.
- Tailored employment support replacing one‑size‑fits‑all schemes; end harsh sanctions on genuine claimants.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC‑based assessment/enforcement plus specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working‑age people; option to invest a year’s payment in insulation.
- Strengthen protection for failed occupational pensions; consult and honour accrued public‑sector pension rights.
- Reduce fraud/error through simplification and prevention.

Housing, local services and environment
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; encourage brownfield reuse via VAT reform; require permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; increase core arts funding with inflation; support grassroots sport.
- Devolve more powers; streamline inspectorates; protect post offices and universal postal service.
- Zero‑waste goal; 60% household recycling within seven years; producer responsibility; climate‑aware planning/building rules.

Transport
- Rail reform with fewer, longer franchises; shift road funds to station safety and key upgrades.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty to zero for least‑polluting cars; expand congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty and VED.
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for pensioners, disabled people, families and youth.
- Limit major new roads; grow rail freight; develop ports/waterways; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new SE expansions.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Fair‑trading duty and Food Trade Inspector to protect farm gate prices.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act with conservation zones and regional co‑management; stronger wildlife protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act.
- Precaution on GM crops, support GM‑free zones, rigorous labelling; promote organic.

Europe, international affairs and defence
- Support EU institutional reform subject to referendum; prepare for euro entry if conditions met.
- Iraq: back democratic transition, build Iraqi capacity, and aim to withdraw forces with UN mandate expiry.
- Multilateral security, UN and EU reform, human rights focus.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reprioritise programmes; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms‑export oversight; back an international arms trade treaty.
- International development: increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; fair trade access; responsible investment; green development priorities; stronger action on global environmental crime; lead on climate targets (Kyoto plus “contraction and convergence”).

Constitution and governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; reduce departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; fair funding across the UK.
- Extend STV to local and national elections; predominantly elected second chamber; voting age aligned with other civic responsibilities; reform BBC governance via an independent regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; merge key portfolios into a single environment/transport/energy department.
